title: Hexane extract of Pittosporopsis kerrii Craib mitigates LPS-driven inflammatory responses via JAK/STAT1 pathway inhibition in RAW 264.7 macrophages.
authors: Anukanon, Shisanupong; Phukhatmuen, Piyaporn; Wanta, Arunothai; Teerapattarakan, Narudol; Hankittichai, Phateep
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物在巨噬细胞中的抗炎作用及对JAK/STAT1通路的抑制，仅含分子对接但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pittosporopsis kerrii Craib is traditionally used to relieve inflammatory conditions, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the anti-inflammatory effects of the hexane extract of P. kerrii (PK-H) in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, with emphasis on STAT1 signaling. METHODS: Cell viability was evaluated using the MTT assay. Anti-inflammatory activity was assessed by measuring nitric oxide (NO) production, inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Activation of NF-kappaB, MAPKs, and STAT1 was examined by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Phytochemical profiling was performed by LC-MS/QTOF, and putative constituents were analyzed by molecular docking against STAT1, JAK1, JAK2, and IFNGR1. RESULTS: PK-H showed low cytotoxicity (CC(5)(0)  approximately  155.4 mug/mL) and significantly inhibited NO production (IC(5)(0)  approximately  15.7 mug/mL). The extract reduced iNOS expression and proinflammatory cytokine release, while not markedly reducing NF-kappaB phosphorylation but partially preserving IkappaB and limiting NF-kappaB nuclear accumulation, despite negligible effect on MAPK activation. In contrast, PK-H markedly suppressed STAT1 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation. LC-MS/QTOF analysis revealed diterpenoids dominated by icacinlactone and icacinol derivatives. Docking studies identified 12-hydroxyicacinlactone A and icacinlactone A as consistent binders to JAK-STAT pathway targets. CONCLUSIONS: PK-H exerts anti-inflammatory effects predominantly through selective inhibition of the JAK-STAT1 pathway. Its diterpenoid constituents represent promising leads for STAT1-targeted anti-inflammatory agents.
abstract_zh: 背景：Pittosporopsis kerrii Craib传统上用于缓解炎症性疾病，但其分子机制尚不清楚。本研究探讨了P. kerrii己烷提取物（PK-H）在脂多糖（LPS）刺激的RAW 264.7巨噬细胞中的抗炎作用，重点关注STAT1信号通路。方法：采用MTT法评估细胞活力。通过测量一氧化氮（NO）产生、诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）、环氧合酶-2（COX-2）、肿瘤坏死因子-α（TNF-α）和白细胞介素-6（IL-6）来评估抗炎活性。通过Western blotting和免疫荧光检测NF-κB、MAPKs和STAT1的激活。采用LC-MS/QTOF进行植物化学分析，并通过分子对接分析推定成分与STAT1、JAK1、JAK2和IFNGR1的结合。结果：PK-H显示出低细胞毒性（CC₅₀约155.4 μg/mL），并显著抑制NO产生（IC₅₀约15.7 μg/mL）。该提取物降低了iNOS表达和促炎细胞因子释放，同时未显著降低NF-κB磷酸化，但部分保留了IκB并限制了NF-κB核积累，尽管对MAPK激活影响可忽略。相反，PK-H显著抑制了STAT1磷酸化和核转位。LC-MS/QTOF分析显示二萜类化合物以icacinlactone和icacinol衍生物为主。对接研究确定12-羟基icacinlactone A和icacinlactone A为JAK-STAT通路靶点的一致结合物。结论：PK-H主要通过选择性抑制JAK-STAT1通路发挥抗炎作用。其二萜类成分代表了针对STAT1的抗炎药物的有前景的先导化合物。
